newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT to defend margins with cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT to defend margins with cost cuts.

text.p: Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV said on Tuesday its PTT Telecom unit would seek to defend its margins in basic telecommunications services by cutting costs.
PTT Telecom managing director Ben Verwaayen said the company would also aim to raise overall volumes, partly through growth in new areas such as Internet and value added services.

Verwaayen told a press briefing that fierce competition was driving down prices for basic services. But PTT Telecom would seek to hold margins steady in traditional telecommunications by pursuing a "drastic reduction" in unit costs, he said.
Verwaayen declined to quantify targets for cost-cutting or revenue growth in new businesses.
But PTT Telecom would gradually halve the number of its telephone exchanges in the Netherlands from 1,300 now, leading to lower costs and faster introduction of new services, he said.
A new Internet business unit will be created in which PTT Telecom will invest some 600 million guilders in the coming years, he said.
